Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs Justice M G Uma
 Oral Order
(Per: Hon'Ble Mrs Justice M G Uma) Petitioners being accused Nos.2 to 4 in Crime
No.5/2024 of Women Police Station, Kalaburagi city, now pending in C.C.No.282/2025 on the file
of the learned I-Additional Civil Judge and Jmfc at Kalaburagi, registered Nc: 2025:Khc-K:5190
Hc-Kar for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of the
Indian Penal Code, 1860 [for short, 'the Ipc'] and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961 [for short, 'the D.P. Act'] are seeking to quash the criminal proceedings.

2. Heard Sri Malik Pasha Mouzan, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Gopalkrishna B.
Yadav, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1. Respondent No.2

though Shabbirmiya vs The State Through on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129384615/
2 served, has remained un- represented.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
Whether the criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioners is liable to be quashed invoking inherent power under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?

Respondent No.2 filed the first information with Women Police Station, Kalaburagi alleging that she married accused No.1 on 11.01.2020 and since then started residing in the matrimonial house along with her husband - accused No.1.
After few days accused No.1 started picking up quarrel under the influence of alcohol and was abusing respondent No.2 that she had not brought sufficient dowry.
He treated her with cruelty.

Respondent No.2 also stated that accused No.2 being the father-in-law,
accused Nos.3 and 4 being the sisters-in- law, started abusing her in filthy language on the same ground and demanded a car and a plot.
They taken away her jewelry and ousted her from matrimonial house.

5. Respondent No.2 contends that on 18.10.2023 at 11.00 p.m., accused No.1 came to the parents'
house of respondent No.2 fully drunk, abused her in filthy language NC: 2025:KHC-K:5190 HC-KAR demanding additional dowry and criminally intimidated her.

Therefore, she lodged the first information on 25.01.2024.
6.
There is inordinate delay in filing the complaint.

Even though specific allegations are made against accused No.1 for having committed the offences, a very bald and general allegations are made against these petitioners being the father-in-law and sisters-in-law of respondent No.2.
It is noticed that accused No.2 is aged 65 years.
It is stated that accused Nos.3 and 4 are the married sisters of accused No.1.
Accused No.3 is said to be the resident of Uttar Pradesh and accused No.4 is said to be the resident of Hyderabad.
Copies of the Adhaar card are produced by the petitioners in that regard.
7. On going through the allegations made by the first informant, her grievance is mainly against accused No.1.
However, she made allegations against these petitioners without reference to any date or time.
The last NC: 2025:KHC-K:5190 HC-KAR incident referred to by her in the first information is dated 18.10.2023 which was committed only by her husband.
But the first information came to be filed on 25.01.2024.
Considering all these facts and circumstances, I am of the opinion that respondent No.2 had filed the first information roping in these petitioners only to pressurize accused No.1.
Therefore, initiation of criminal proceedings and continuation of the same against them is in abuse of process of law.
Hence, the same is liable to be quashed.

Accordingly, I answer the Shabbirmiya vs The State Through on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129384615/
3 above point in the 'affirmative' and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Criminal Petition is allowed.

(ii) Criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioners (accused Nos.2 to 4) in Crime No.5/2024 of Women Police Station, Kalaburagi city, pending in C.C.No.282/
2025, on the file of learned I-Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Kalaburagi, for the NC: 2025:KHC-K:5190 HC-KAR offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504,
506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 is hereby quashed.
Sd/-
